note: Back for fall. Moved to low-sodium beef stock after residents said it ran salty.
Our BBQ night favorite. We'd like it in the Kisco library so other communities can run it.

recipe.name: Carolina Meatloaf
recipe.menuDescriptor: Smoked paprika meatloaf with a tangy Carolina BBQ glaze, mashed potatoes and collards
method: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Mix the beef, breadcrumbs, egg, onion and paprika. Do not overmix.
Form loaves in hotel pans and bake 45 minutes.
Brush with BBQ sauce and bake 10 more minutes to set the glaze.
Rest 10 minutes. Slice 1 inch thick. Hold hot at 140°F or above.
plating: Mashed potatoes at 10 o'clock, collards at 2 o'clock.
Slice leaning on the potatoes, glaze spooned over.
recipe.cookNotes: Glaze in the last 10 minutes only. 160°F internal before resting.
recipe.variations: Mechanical soft: chop the slice and serve the glaze on the side. Lower sodium: halve the BBQ sauce and add apple cider vinegar.

note: Milder chile for residents who found it too hot, and a gluten-friendly binder so more residents can have it.

recipe.name: Green Chile Meatloaf
recipe.menuDescriptor: Meatloaf with roasted Hatch green chile and a cotija crumble, with Spanish rice

ingredients.name: roasted mild Hatch green chile, diced

method: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Mix the beef, oats, egg, chile and cumin. Do not overmix.
Form loaves in hotel pans and bake 45 minutes to 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes. Slice 1 inch thick.
Top each slice with cotija just before it goes out.
plating: Slice at 6 o'clock, cotija and cilantro on top.
recipe.cookNotes: Taste the chile batch: if it is hot, use half and add roasted poblano for the rest.

note: New soup for the fall menu. Vegetarian and dairy-free as written; cream optional on the side.

recipe.name: Butternut Squash Bisque
recipe.menuDescriptor: Velvety roasted butternut squash bisque with apple and a whisper of sage
recipe.garnish: Toasted pepitas and a sage leaf
method: Toss the squash in oil and roast at 400°F for 30 minutes until browned at the edges.
Sweat the onion and apple 5 minutes.
Add the squash, stock and sage. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend smooth with an immersion blender. Thin with stock if needed.
Hold hot at 140°F or above.
plating: Pepitas in a line across the top, sage leaf at the end.
recipe.cookNotes: Blend fully: no strings for residents on a puree diet.

note: A no-sugar-added dessert so residents watching their blood sugar have a warm choice. Tested with our diabetic residents' council.

recipe.name: No Sugar Added Apple Crisp
recipe.desc: Cinnamon apples, oat and pecan topping
recipe.menuDescriptor: Warm cinnamon apple crisp with an oat and pecan topping, sweetened with fruit only
recipe.garnish: Dollop of whipped topping, sugar free

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced

method: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the apples with the juice concentrate, cinnamon and lemon. Spread in a buttered half hotel pan.
Rub the oats, flour, pecans and butter together to coarse crumbs. Scatter over the apples.
Bake 40 minutes until the apples are tender and the top is golden.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut 4 x 3. Hold warm at 140°F or above.
plating: Square in the center of a small warm plate.
Whipped topping on the corner, not on top, so the crumble stays crisp.
recipe.cookNotes: Pureed diet: blend the apples and serve the topping on the side.
recipe.variations: Nut free: leave out the pecans and add 1 more tbsp of oats.

note: Our take on the Kisco meatloaf for the Southwest menu.
comment: Approved. Great use of Hatch chile. Keep an eye on the heat for residents who prefer mild.

Rest 10 minutes. Slice 1 inch thick.
Top each slice with cotija just before it goes out.

note: Summer special that residents asked to keep.
comment: Approved as written. Clear plating notes.

method: Brown the beef and drain. Set aside.
Sweat the onion, carrot and celery in butter 6 minutes.
Add the flour and cook 2 minutes for a blond roux.
Whisk in the stock. Add the potatoes and simmer until tender, about 20 minutes.
Return the beef. Stir in the milk, then the cheese a handful at a time, below a boil.
Season with the salt. Hold hot at 140°F or above.

comment: Approved. Watch the sodium: it is close to the soup cap.

note: Turkey meatloaf with a teriyaki glaze for our lighter-fare night.
comment: Sodium is 1,450 mg a serving; the Kisco cap for an entrée is 900 mg. Use low-sodium soy, drop the bouillon, and send it again.

recipe.name: Teriyaki Turkey Meatloaf
recipe.menuDescriptor: Ginger turkey meatloaf with a teriyaki glaze and steamed jasmine rice
method: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Mix the turkey, panko, egg, ginger and bouillon.
Form loaves and bake 40 minutes.
Glaze with teriyaki and bake 10 more minutes to 165°F.
plating: Slice at 6 o'clock, sesame and scallion on top.
recipe.cookNotes: Glaze in the last 10 minutes. 165°F internal before resting.

note: Sunday brunch special. Soft grits so residents on a mechanical soft diet can have it with the shrimp chopped.
comment: Shrimp is a shellfish allergen: tick Shellfish so the servers and the kitchen ticket warn. Add a hold temperature for the grits, then send it again.

recipe.name: Shrimp and Pimento Cheese Grits
recipe.menuDescriptor: Sautéed Gulf shrimp over creamy pimento cheese grits with a little smoked tomato gravy
method: Bring the water and milk to a simmer. Whisk in the grits and cook low 35 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in the pimento cheese and butter off the heat.
Season the shrimp and sauté 2 minutes a side, to 145°F.
Warm the tomato gravy.
plating: Grits in the center of a warm shallow bowl.
Shrimp fanned on top, gravy spooned around.
recipe.cookNotes: Mechanical soft: chop the shrimp to 1/4 inch.
